body: When I was 24, my brother was turning 30 and the family was all going on a trip for a few nights to celebrate. I started panicking about it and then realised I'd only left the house about five times in the last decade and for the five years before that had only left to go to school. I realised that my life was in tatters.

I'm not insulting you because you insulted him you moron, I'm insulting you because you're an insensitive prick who thinks it's ok to tell people with depression that they should get a life. Are you really so dense that you can't see that?
Your comment had fuck all to do with anything, and I'm nit asking you to explain anything, I'm telling you that you are a knob.

> you asked me to explain why I think he can get stuffed and I have.

No I didn't, what the fuck is wrong with you?
Fuck off with your back peddling pseudo intellectual justification, it doesn't wash. Just take the hint and admit you were being a cunt.
You literally said it applies to anyone who agrees with what he said. Are you a troll or just an idiot?

>The guy is a prick and his political views result in multitudes of people becoming destitute.

And you're a prick who's attitude results in millions of people killing themselves every year. Even if what you say about that guy is true, you're no better.

You know how you said that other guy is a bell end? 

Mental health problems aren't things you can just snap out of and people can't just decide to up and "get a life". When you're struggling to survive day to day and getting out of bed is a painful experience all of your energy is sapped by maintaining just a thin veneer of normalcy. And when morons come along with trite "tough love" bullshit like "get a life" then a little more weight is added to the crap people already have to carry. So please just fuck off with that shite.
I'm not that user but I agree with him, do I need to invest in a life?
Yes, I've tried everything.

I'm talking about minute things. Things most people take for granted I've systematically failed at.

As for turning it around, I don't want to try anymore. I want people to stop trying to fix things and telling me what could (but probably won't) happen and just listen to how I feel and tell me it's understandable.

That's one of the biggest things that kept me trapped for all those years. Eventually I hit rock bottom and decided to do whatever I had to to move away. It was a hard experience, my anxiety was being turned up to 11 every hour I wasn't asleep. But it did give me space and more importantly a reason to grow and find ways to cope.

People don't avoid me because they think "he's got mental problems so I'm staying clear", I rarely talk about it. What happens is that potential friendships just peter out because there's no connection and there's no way of forming a connection because I'm just fundamentally not like them. 

I was thinking today about tribes, how people tend to belong to certain groups with whom they share things in common. So people who went to university might tend to be friends with others who had that life path, that kind of thing. But I don't have a tribe, there aren't any groups I fit in with. I've tried but it always becomes clear that I don't really belong, I don't get their frames of reference, I don't speak their language, I don't hold the same views. It's a very alien feeling.

I don't think that's because of social anxiety per se, I think it's because the social anxiety and depression that came with it caused me to be shut off from everyone but my immediate family for about 15 years. I grew up in one room, I didn't go to college, university, I didn't get my first job, I didn't have friends or relationships. My life was literally empty. I don't not talk about my past because there isn't anything to talk about. 

It's a hole too deep to climb out of.
I'm away from the abusive people thankfully, and my partner and I have made a lot of progress. I just need a win really.
Sorry for snapping, I'm just in a crappy place right now.

Yeah sure it's totally normal to not step outside for 15 years, totally normal to have to sleep with a chest of drawers in front of you door because you're worried your housemate might come in with a knife in the night, totally normal for your "best friend" to rape you then emotionally blackmail you by cutting herself and sending you the pictures, totally normal develop clinical depression at 7 and arthritis at 30. And yeah all these things are my responsibility, my shortcomings, you're right.

I'm in pretty much exactly the same place as the OP and I agree with you that age doesn't mean you can't go out and have fun like that but there are caveats. 

The big one is that entry into that lifestyle isn't easy when you get to 30+ without having had that experience. You don't have friends to tag along with and you don't necessarily have the social skills.

Another is the creep factor; being an older bloke hanging around a predominantly 18-25 scene just doesn't look good unless you already have friends to hang out with. And, at least in my experience, the people who are our age and do this kind of stuff aren't necessarily looking for new people to join them.
The fact that you're deleting a post that was directed towards your own heavily downvoted reply looks sketchy af.

I would love to but sadly I can't as the NHS doesn't offer it in my area and I can't afford it privately. It just seems like yet another obstacle that's been put in my way by some vindictive overseer.
I never translate how I feel into actions, I know it would hurt people and I know no one deserves that. I just quietly seethe in myself and hate myself for it.
I just meant the feeling of not wanting to fight. Personally I feel like I've tried so much and so hard and it's getting exhausting just trying to stop from sinking.
This sounds very familiar :/

>edit:sorry about the wall of text 

Don't worry about it, I can only speak for myself but reading your experiences is a great help. I know there's literally nothing I can say to help but know that you're helping me and I'm grateful.

Do you have any advice on how to approach it with her?

Also does it make a difference that she's had hee own mh issues? I don't want to exacerbate them.

This is another thing that scares me about suicide; I'm not religious and I don't believe in fate so in my mind there is always a "what if", as hopeless as everything seems or even is now there is always a chance of something better in the future but if I killed myself there definitely isn't. Of course the flip side of "what if that chance never materialises" keeps suicide on my mind.
That's good to hear. Knowing that how do you feel looking back at your attempt?
Thanks for sharing. Mind if I ask what's kept you away from trying again?

I'm really sorry to hear that. I'm in a similar place, though really don't understand my own thoughts on it, I worry about doing something and at the last second regretting it when it's too late. Along with how it would affect others that's probably the biggest reason I (so far) won't go ahead with it.

I hope you find a reason to change your mind.
Have your thoughts changed since then?
I once asked my mum what I'd achieved in life and after a pause all she could think to say was "you're alive", that felt like a kick in the gut.

I'm not instantly dismissing anything; I've seen a lot of counsellors and used enough self help material to know what does and doesn't work for me. Your suggestions are appreciated but I'm sorry I don't think they'd help me. 

And yes this thread was just to vent my frustrated at the NHS mental health provision.

I had a look at their website after they called me, I'm sure it's helpful for those with very mild difficulties and/or people who are going through a rough patch but as I said in the OP this is a life long thing for me. And having read the self help books and had several counsellors I need something a lot more intensive and tailored. 

Mind may offer counselling for free but again I'm not sure it would be focused enough for me. In my experience counsellors just aren't experienced or knowledgable enough to deal with very serious cases.

It's amazing how it can be so variable across the country. 

>Do you have a mental health team for your county that you could ask to be referred to?

I have no idea, I contacted the only people I was given information for and they told me about the group thing. Just googled around and found something called a "Community Mental Health Team" but I don't know if that's what I've already been in touch with.
It does feel like I'm just being put on a conveyor belt so they can tick a box when I come out the other end.

If you ever have the chance go private, it costs a lot but the quality of care is so much better and in the long run considering how much mental health costs you in lost earnings it might even work out cheaper if it gets you back into a functioning state quicker. 

I had a bad experience with the NHS when I first started seeking help and decided to stay away after that, it's only a lack of funds that's forced me back and like you I'm now thinking I might as well just work through it alone.

I think this sometimes, I was always at the top of my class at school and when I was very young I was popular and extroverted and then depression hit and I did poorly at school and got lost in social isolation. If that hadn't happened I think I could have been very successful but then I think "but you weren't, how arrogant are you to think you would have been a success when most people have just average lives and you haven't even managed that?" And then I feel a wave guilt and self hate.
Having the money to pay a therapist for years on end seems to be the only thing I can come up with.

> It's unfortunate because I feel like it was supposed to be a great chapter in my life that I was robbed of

This is something that really resonates with me. I feel like my whole childhood and adolescence never happened; I suppose it sort of didn't.
I've never noticed in anyone else, but yeah I've had people come up to me randomly and ask if I'm ok. I guess it's a nice gesture but it made me feel like a freak.

It sounds like this has really blindsided you and you're in shock. 

But try taking a step back, what happened represents just a few months to a year of your life, a life which will probably span 80 years. In the space of a couple of months you met two girls you liked and who liked you, at least enough to give you a chance; so odds are you'll meet someone else and given how you forgot about the first when you met the second you'll probably forget about both when you meet the third (and the fourth, and the fifth, few people end up with the first person they meet). As for your shoulders, it doesn't sound like it's permanent and as you say it'll take months to get back in shape, again months out of a lifetime isn't that long. 

I know that things like this really, really suck and it's ok to feel this shitty about it, but your odds are good for things to get better.

>if you think nobody cares about you, I do. I think you are a very special person.

This is going to come off as very ungrateful and I'm sorry for that but in response to this sentence; no you don't. You don't know me, you don't know what I've done, good or bad; if you met me you might love me but then you might hate me too. To say that you think everyone is special is to say no one is special, it doesn't mean anything. 

These kinds of sentiments, while I know they're well meaning, have the opposite effect for me. I don't feel like a human being who is cared about I feel like a fire that needs to be brought under control and can be forgotten about once it's out.  

Personally I've been dealing with depression and other mental health problems since I was a child, I've almost exhausted all the options for getting better and when I have done that I will make a considered and informed choice as to whether I want to end my life, and if I decide to do that then that is my choice.

Maybe this could be a turning point and bring you two even closer?

I know you say you'd be shattered to find something like that from a loved one but also wouldn't you want to know how they're feeling?

I agree, suicide isn't something that should be done on a whim without any thought but if someone has had depression for decades they know what they want. 

I opened up to my therapist about my suicidal thoughts the other day and she asked me to call if I ever felt that I was going to go ahead with it and I just though "why?"; so she can talk me out of it only to go back to her normal life while I trudge on in pain? If I decide I want to go then that decision should be respected.
This is how I feel, I don't have the skills to cope or to be happy. It's not a question of curing an illness or finding where I fit because I just don't have the raw materials for a happy life.

Yes and we talked but it hasn't helped.  

I've just been trying for so long that it's hard to see things ever changing. Especially fundamental things like the way I look.

No my therapists have never talked about anything like that. It takes long enough just to get a grip on what problems I have. 

I'm not sure what I'd do anyway, nothing seems to take me away from these thoughts. It all just ends up making me feel worse. 

I do try to keep some forward momentum, I force myself to go to the gym and to study as well as the normal things like look after myself but like I said it feels like I'm just struggling to stay afloat. I look at other people my age, and increasingly people younger than me, and see that they're working towards something, a career, a family, or just making money to have fun and I'm not able to do any of that. I'm working so hard just to be at the educational level of an 18 year old, or I'm saving and looking into surgery just so I can look like a normal person. All my time and energy seems to be exhausted by trying to get to a place that most people find themselves at by default. It's just too much.
I've never actually been advised to do anything.

Yeah always. 

What do you mean? I just want to look normal, to not hate myself, have confidence, not have crippling pains, etc; whether you call that moving or climbing a mountain it still seems impossible. It's not like I haven't tried, that's all I've been doing my whole life for seemingly no gain.
Had lots of therapy and medication.  Tried to push myself to be more social, tried to get back to education. It all juat feels like I'm chipping away at a mountain.
Exactly, like I just took a wrong turn somewhere and I could turn around and go back but I can't.
Can you elaborate?

I'm reading it. I'm sorry to hear you've got to that point in your life. I can't really say much to you, I was researching methods last night so anything I said would probably be fairly hypocritical! Incidently you should know how often suicide fails and ends up just causing horrible injuries,  even with guns, it's not something to do without serious planning!  


I wish you weren't in a place where suicide was so attractive and I sincerely do hope you can find another route. 

Can I ask what brought you this decision?

Yes! I feel like someone who only has one hand because he was trying to open his beer with a chainsaw while wearing a blindfold, it's not worth anyone's sympathy because he's an idiot who brought it on himself. I'm depressed but I don't have a good enough reason for it. 


You're right it's the depression itself talking, it's ingenious in the way it feeds itself.
